provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Phonics: long vowels
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify long vowel sounds.
The pupils should be able to spell magic e words.
Introduction:
Today we will learn about long vowels. We know short sounds from last term.
Content:
Long vowels say their name. Magic e makes vowels long. Cake has a long a sound. Kite has a long i sound. Home has a long o sound. Tube has a long u sound. The e at the end is silent but makes the vowel long.
Class activity:
Pupils will read words with magic e from the board.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does the a make in cake?
Spell a word with a long o sound.
What does the magic e do?
Summary:
Today we learned about long vowels and magic e words.

topics.title: Comprehension: the farm
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read a passage about the farm.
The pupils should be able to answer questions about the passage.
Introduction:
We have read many stories before. Today we will read about a farm.
Content:
The passage is about a farm with animals. It tells us what the farmer does. We need to read carefully to understand. Look for key words like cow, hen, and crops.
Class activity:
Pupils will read the passage in pairs and answer questions together.
Evaluation questions:
What animals are on the farm?
What does the farmer grow?
Where do the hens lay eggs?
Summary:
We practiced reading and understanding a farm passage.

topics.title: Grammar: prepositions
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list prepositions.
The pupils should be able to use prepositions correctly.
Introduction:
We know words that show where things are. Today we will learn more about them.
Content:
Prepositions show position. In means inside something. On means on top of something. Under means below something. Between means in the middle of two things.
Class activity:
Pupils will place objects in different positions and say sentences using prepositions.
Evaluation questions:
Where is the book? It is ___ the table.
Show me something between two chairs.
What preposition shows inside?
Summary:
Today we learned about prepositions for position.

topics.title: Grammar: tenses
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify different tenses.
The pupils should be able to change sentences between tenses.
Introduction:
We talk about things happening now, before, and later. Today we learn how to show this.
Content:
Today is for now. Yesterday is for before. Tomorrow is for later. We change words to show time. I eat today. I ate yesterday. I will eat tomorrow.
Class activity:
Pupils will change sentences from today to yesterday and tomorrow.
Evaluation questions:
Change this sentence to yesterday: I play football.
What tense shows future?
What word shows past tense?
Summary:
We learned how to show different times using tenses.

topics.title: Vocabulary: word building
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add s, ed and ing to words.
The pupils should be able to build new words.
Introduction:
We can make new words by adding letters. Today we will practice this.
Content:
Adding s makes words plural. Adding ed makes past tense. Adding ing makes present continuous. Walk becomes walks, walked, walking. Talk becomes talks, talked, talking.
Class activity:
Pupils will take base words and add s, ed and ing to make new words.
Evaluation questions:
What word do you get by adding s to cat?
Change jump to past tense.
What does adding ing show?
Summary:
Today we learned how to build new words by adding letters.

topics.title: Composition: a rainy day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write a four sentence story.
The pupils should be able to use first, then, last in writing.
Introduction:
We have read many stories. Today we will write our own story about rain.
Content:
A good story has beginning, middle, end. First tells the start. Then tells what happened next. Last tells how it ended. Use simple sentences.
Class activity:
Pupils will write a four sentence story about a rainy day using first, then, last.
Evaluation questions:
What word tells the start of your story?
What word tells the middle?
How many sentences did you write?
Summary:
We practiced writing a short story with beginning, middle, end.

topics.title: Letter writing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write a letter to a friend.
The pupils should be able to use greeting and closing correctly.
Introduction:
Sometimes we write letters to people who are far away. Today we will learn how.
Content:
A letter has parts. Greeting is at the start like Dear Friend. Closing is at the end like From Your Name. We write about things we want to share.
Class activity:
Pupils will write a letter to a friend in the class with proper greeting and closing.
Evaluation questions:
What do you write at the start of a letter?
What do you write at the end?
What is between greeting and closing?
Summary:
Today we learned how to write a letter to a friend.

topics.title: Handwriting and dictation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to copy a paragraph neatly.
The pupils should be able to write from dictation.
Introduction:
Good writing is easy to read. Today we will practice our handwriting.
Content:
We copy a paragraph carefully. We sit properly and hold our pencil right. For dictation, we listen carefully and write what the teacher says.
Class activity:
Pupils will copy a paragraph from the board and then do a full dictation.
Evaluation questions:
How should you hold your pencil?
What do you need to do during dictation?
Why is good handwriting important?
Summary:
We practiced copying and writing from dictation.

topics.title: Spelling drill
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to spell words correctly.
The pupils should be able to participate in a spelling bee.
Introduction:
Spelling is important for good writing. Today we will practice spelling words.
Content:
Look, cover, write, check helps us learn words. Look at the word, cover it, write it, check if correct. A spelling bee is a game where we spell words one by one.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice look, cover, write, check with difficult words and then have a class spelling bee.
Evaluation questions:
What are the four steps in look, cover, write, check?
Spell the word friend.
What is a spelling bee?
Summary:
Today we practiced spelling words using different methods.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall what we learned this term.
The pupils should be able to complete the end of year quiz.
Introduction:
We have learned many things this term. Today we will revise and see what we remember.
Content:
We will go over all topics: phonics, comprehension, grammar, vocabulary, composition, letter writing, handwriting, spelling. We need to remember everything for the quiz.
Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to revise topics and then take the end of year quiz individually.
Evaluation questions:
What are long vowels?
Give an example of a preposition.
How do you change a word to past tense?
What is the greeting in a letter?
Summary:
We revised all topics and took the end of year quiz.
